- Chemistry-led product innovation - custom steel compositions balanced for specific performance needs, described by management as the single biggest driver of the year's results and a genuine point of differentiation
- Preferred-vendor status with Tier-2 OEM suppliers giving recurring rather than one-off orders, and customer loyalty that management says does not waver when market prices do
- Performance-linked pricing that reduces dependence on general market price movements
- Maintained 100% capacity utilization through the year
- Tight control over power costs, scrap sourcing and yield losses, which management links directly to quarter-over-quarter margin expansion
- Vaneera's advanced metallurgy (LRF, VD, EMS) positions its alloy steel as a substitute for arc-furnace steel at roughly a 5-10% lower price point, addressing an underserved mid-premium segment between bulk mild steel and premium EAF output
- Manufacturing on 100% recycled scrap as raw material
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Steel price cyclicality driven by global oversupply and weak Chinese demand — The MD&A's entire 'RISK AND CONCERNS' section is a single paragraph naming this: 'Global oversupply, softened demand from China, ongoing wars and volatile input and freight costs continued to weigh on benchmark prices.' Benchmark price weakness is what forced the company to choose margin over volume, and it is outside management's control.
- Volatile input and freight costs; margin depends on scrap and power cost control — Management flags volatile input and freight costs in the same Risk and Concerns paragraph, and separately attributes the year's margin expansion to 'tight control over power costs, scrap sourcing, and yield losses'. Since the company manufactures on 100% recycled scrap, scrap and power price moves feed straight through to the margin story the equity case now rests on.
- Geopolitical disruption — 'Ongoing wars' is named by management as one of the factors weighing on benchmark prices, alongside freight cost volatility - both are exogenous and were flagged as continuing rather than resolved.
- No capacity headroom in the existing business — The company reports it 'maintained 100% capacity utilization through the year'. With the base plant already full, incremental growth cannot come from the existing asset and depends entirely on the new alloy steel capacity being commissioned.
- Execution and ramp-up risk on the Vaneera alloy steel project — The FY27 growth plan rests on one project: phase 1 of 100,000 MT per annum at Vaneera Industries' Ludhiana facility is stated only as 'ready to commission soon', with alloy steel facility work still 'underway' and no commissioning date, no rupee capex quantum and no funding plan disclosed in the report. The full 204,000 MT per annum licensed capacity is described as four times the company's current capacity, so the ramp is large relative to the existing business.
- Rising leverage after the acquisition — In its key-ratio disclosure the company explains the movement in its debt-equity ratio and debt service coverage ratio as being 'due to Increase in Borrowings during the year as compared to previous year' and 'Increase in the amount of Borrowings and their repayments during the year'. Borrowings rose from a near-debt-free base in a year in which the balance of the Vaneera consideration was paid, and further alloy-steel phases are still to be funded.
- Concentration in a narrow set of end markets and Tier-2 OEM customers — The value-added strategy deliberately concentrates the book on automotive, agri-machinery, engineering and precision industrial buyers, with the company 'established as a preferred vendor to Tier-2 OEM suppliers'. The same recurring-order relationships that support realisations also make the business sensitive to a downturn in auto and engineering demand; the report discloses no customer-concentration numbers.
- Single-location operations and a very small workforce — Both the existing business and the new alloy steel facility are at Ludhiana, Punjab, and the report states 'During the year, the company has employed 55 persons.' A single manufacturing location and a headcount that small leave the company exposed to site-level disruption and to key-person dependence on the promoter-family executive directors.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Garg Furnace Limited manufactures steel using 100% recycled scrap as its raw material and supplies custom steel compositions in which carbon, manganese and chromium are balanced for specific performance needs. Its customers are auto component suppliers, agricultural equipment makers, engineering and precision industrial buyers, where it is established as a preferred vendor to Tier-2 OEM suppliers on recurring rather than one-off orders. Through its 51%-owned subsidiary Vaneera Industries Limited it is moving into alloy steel billets produced on a Ladle Refining Furnace, Vacuum Degassing and Electro-Magnetic Stirrer route for quality-sensitive end markets.

outlook.body:
- Shift from a commodity mindset to a value-first, margin-driven model - management frames FY26 as the year the strategy 'stopped being a plan and became a track record', with profit growth deliberately outpacing revenue growth
- Chemistry-led product innovation at scale - balancing carbon, manganese and chromium into custom compositions, described as the single biggest driver of the year's results and the company's main point of differentiation
- Move the product mix away from commodity steel toward specialised, performance-led grades for automotive, agri-machinery, engineering and precision industrial applications, so that each tonne moved up the value chain is less exposed to industry price swings
- Build an alloy steel platform through the completed acquisition of a 51% controlling stake in Vaneera Industries Ltd., adding advanced metallurgy (LRF, VD, EMS), capacity and customer access in auto, engineering, railways and defence-grade markets
- Position Vaneera/GFL alloy steel as a substitute for arc-furnace steel at roughly a 5-10% lower price point, targeting the underserved mid-premium segment between bulk mild steel and premium EAF output, including an import substitution opportunity in premium alloy grades
- Extend from auto and engineering into railways and defence-grade requirements
- Deepen the preferred-vendor relationship with Tier-2 OEM suppliers to convert one-off orders into recurring business, supported by performance-linked pricing
- Continue manufacturing on 100% recycled scrap as raw material
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The only expansion project the FY2025-26 annual report describes is the alloy steel platform acquired through Vaneera Industries Limited (formerly Vaneera Industries Private Limited), in which Garg Furnace Ltd. acquired a 51% controlling stake; the Directors' Report records the subsidiary as acquired on 21.08.2025 and the MD&A records the acquisition as completed with 'alloy steel facility work underway'. Vaneera has built a licensed induction-furnace alloy steel facility at Ludhiana, Punjab, equipped with a Ladle Refining Furnace (LRF) for precise temperature control and impurity removal, Vacuum Degassing (VD) for superior cleanliness and lower hydrogen/oxygen content, and an Electro-Magnetic Stirrer (EMS) for uniform grain structure, producing alloy steel billets for quality-sensitive end markets. Licensed capacity is stated as 204,000 MT per annum of alloy steel, described as 4 times GFL's current capacity, with project status given as 'phase 1 of 100,000 MT per annum is ready to commission soon' - no commissioning date and no rupee capex quantum are disclosed anywhere in the routed text. Target sectors are automobile, auto components, general engineering and railways, with strategic fit extending toward defence-grade applications, and the output is positioned as a substitute for arc-furnace steel at roughly a 5-10% lower price point, opening an underserved mid-premium segment and an import substitution opportunity in premium alloy grades. On the existing base the company reports it maintained 100% capacity utilization through the year; no absolute installed capacity for Garg Furnace's own plant is disclosed, only the relative statement that Vaneera's licensed capacity is four times it.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Industry backdrop is difficult: global oversupply, softened demand from China, ongoing wars and volatile input and freight costs continued to weigh on benchmark steel prices
- Management's stated response is to refuse volume at falling prices and lean further into performance-led steel, which it credits for profit growing nearly four times faster than revenue
- Performance-linked pricing continued to reduce dependence on general market price movements
- Margin lever: tight control over power costs, scrap sourcing and yield losses translated directly into margin expansion quarter over quarter
- Mix lever: value-added grades are no longer a pilot but a growing share of the order book, commanding better realisations and customer loyalty that management says does not waver when market prices do
- Capacity was fully used - 100% capacity utilization maintained through the year - so incremental growth is expected to come from Vaneera's alloy steel capacity rather than the existing base
- Industry structure: the global Industrial Steel Furnace market is projected to grow from $22.88 billion in 2025 to $36.41 billion by 2034, driven by automotive, construction and aerospace demand, with Electric Arc Furnaces the dominant technology and a shift toward energy-efficient equipment, automation and digitalization
- Vaneera gives direct access to auto, engineering, railways and defence sectors and an import substitution opportunity in premium alloy grades
- Value-added grades are described as 'a growing share of our order book, commanding better realizations'
- Established as a preferred vendor to Tier-2 OEM suppliers, with recurring rather than one-off orders
- Vaneera is described as well suited to import substitution and large OEM contracts (no quantified order book disclosed)

- Vaneera Industries Limited (formerly known as Vaneera Industries Private Limited) — subsidiary: Extent of shareholding 51.22%; became a subsidiary w.e.f. 21.08.2025. Operates a licensed induction-furnace alloy steel facility at Ludhiana, Punjab. Transactions during the year with the company comprised purchase of goods, acquisition of equity shares, sales of goods, a corporate guarantee received, payment of a corporate guarantee fee and rent received. The acquisition of the 51.22% equity stake (58,50,000 equity shares at Rs 62 per share, face value Rs 10 plus premium Rs 52) was approved by the Board on 7th September 2024 and by shareholders at the AGM held on 30th September 2024, with the valuation carried out by a registered valuer; the investment is measured at amortised cost under Ind AS 109.
- Avtar Exports Private Limited — related party: Enterprise over which Key Management Personnel and relatives of such personnel are able to exercise significant influence or control; commission was paid to it during the year.
- Devinder Garg — related party: Key Management Personnel - Managing Director.
- Toshak Garg — related party: Key Management Personnel - Managing Director w.e.f. 14.08.2024.
- Vaneera Garg — related party: Key Management Personnel - Whole-time Director.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Steel:** Custom / chemistry-led steel compositions (carbon, manganese and chromium balanced for specific performance needs), Value-added, performance-led steel grades
- **Alloy steel (through Vaneera Industries Ltd.):** Alloy steel billets produced via LRF + VD + EMS

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Automotive and auto components (Tier-1 and Tier-2 OEM suppliers)
- Agricultural / agri-machinery equipment makers
- General engineering
- Precision industrial customers
- Railways
- Defence-grade applications (stated strategic extension)
- Import substitution in premium alloy grades

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Industry backdrop is difficult: global oversupply, softened demand from China, ongoing wars and volatile input and freight costs continued to weigh on benchmark steel prices
- Management's stated response is to refuse volume at falling prices and lean further into performance-led steel, which it credits for profit growing nearly four times faster than revenue
- Performance-linked pricing continued to reduce dependence on general market price movements
- Margin lever: tight control over power costs, scrap sourcing and yield losses translated directly into margin expansion quarter over quarter
- Mix lever: value-added grades are no longer a pilot but a growing share of the order book, commanding better realisations and customer loyalty that management says does not waver when market prices do
- Capacity was fully used - 100% capacity utilization maintained through the year - so incremental growth is expected to come from Vaneera's alloy steel capacity rather than the existing base
- Industry structure: the global Industrial Steel Furnace market is projected to grow from $22.88 billion in 2025 to $36.41 billion by 2034, driven by automotive, construction and aerospace demand, with Electric Arc Furnaces the dominant technology and a shift toward energy-efficient equipment, automation and digitalization
- Vaneera gives direct access to auto, engineering, railways and defence sectors and an import substitution opportunity in premium alloy grades
- Value-added grades are described as 'a growing share of our order book, commanding better realizations'
- Established as a preferred vendor to Tier-2 OEM suppliers, with recurring rather than one-off orders
- Vaneera is described as well suited to import substitution and large OEM contracts (no quantified order book disclosed)

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Shift from a commodity mindset to a value-first, margin-driven model - management frames FY26 as the year the strategy 'stopped being a plan and became a track record', with profit growth deliberately outpacing revenue growth
- Chemistry-led product innovation at scale - balancing carbon, manganese and chromium into custom compositions, described as the single biggest driver of the year's results and the company's main point of differentiation
- Move the product mix away from commodity steel toward specialised, performance-led grades for automotive, agri-machinery, engineering and precision industrial applications, so that each tonne moved up the value chain is less exposed to industry price swings
- Build an alloy steel platform through the completed acquisition of a 51% controlling stake in Vaneera Industries Ltd., adding advanced metallurgy (LRF, VD, EMS), capacity and customer access in auto, engineering, railways and defence-grade markets
- Position Vaneera/GFL alloy steel as a substitute for arc-furnace steel at roughly a 5-10% lower price point, targeting the underserved mid-premium segment between bulk mild steel and premium EAF output, including an import substitution opportunity in premium alloy grades
- Extend from auto and engineering into railways and defence-grade requirements
- Deepen the preferred-vendor relationship with Tier-2 OEM suppliers to convert one-off orders into recurring business, supported by performance-linked pricing
- Continue manufacturing on 100% recycled scrap as raw material

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The only expansion project the FY2025-26 annual report describes is the alloy steel platform acquired through Vaneera Industries Limited (formerly Vaneera Industries Private Limited), in which Garg Furnace Ltd. acquired a 51% controlling stake; the Directors' Report records the subsidiary as acquired on 21.08.2025 and the MD&A records the acquisition as completed with 'alloy steel facility work underway'. Vaneera has built a licensed induction-furnace alloy steel facility at Ludhiana, Punjab, equipped with a Ladle Refining Furnace (LRF) for precise temperature control and impurity removal, Vacuum Degassing (VD) for superior cleanliness and lower hydrogen/oxygen content, and an Electro-Magnetic Stirrer (EMS) for uniform grain structure, producing alloy steel billets for quality-sensitive end markets. Licensed capacity is stated as 204,000 MT per annum of alloy steel, described as 4 times GFL's current capacity, with project status given as 'phase 1 of 100,000 MT per annum is ready to commission soon' - no commissioning date and no rupee capex quantum are disclosed anywhere in the routed text. Target sectors are automobile, auto components, general engineering and railways, with strategic fit extending toward defence-grade applications, and the output is positioned as a substitute for arc-furnace steel at roughly a 5-10% lower price point, opening an underserved mid-premium segment and an import substitution opportunity in premium alloy grades. On the existing base the company reports it maintained 100% capacity utilization through the year; no absolute installed capacity for Garg Furnace's own plant is disclosed, only the relative statement that Vaneera's licensed capacity is four times it.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Chemistry-led product innovation - custom steel compositions balanced for specific performance needs, described by management as the single biggest driver of the year's results and a genuine point of differentiation
- Preferred-vendor status with Tier-2 OEM suppliers giving recurring rather than one-off orders, and customer loyalty that management says does not waver when market prices do
- Performance-linked pricing that reduces dependence on general market price movements
- Maintained 100% capacity utilization through the year
- Tight control over power costs, scrap sourcing and yield losses, which management links directly to quarter-over-quarter margin expansion
- Vaneera's advanced metallurgy (LRF, VD, EMS) positions its alloy steel as a substitute for arc-furnace steel at roughly a 5-10% lower price point, addressing an underserved mid-premium segment between bulk mild steel and premium EAF output
- Manufacturing on 100% recycled scrap as raw material

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Steel price cyclicality driven by global oversupply and weak Chinese demand — The MD&A's entire 'RISK AND CONCERNS' section is a single paragraph naming this: 'Global oversupply, softened demand from China, ongoing wars and volatile input and freight costs continued to weigh on benchmark prices.' Benchmark price weakness is what forced the company to choose margin over volume, and it is outside management's control.
- Volatile input and freight costs; margin depends on scrap and power cost control — Management flags volatile input and freight costs in the same Risk and Concerns paragraph, and separately attributes the year's margin expansion to 'tight control over power costs, scrap sourcing, and yield losses'. Since the company manufactures on 100% recycled scrap, scrap and power price moves feed straight through to the margin story the equity case now rests on.
- Geopolitical disruption — 'Ongoing wars' is named by management as one of the factors weighing on benchmark prices, alongside freight cost volatility - both are exogenous and were flagged as continuing rather than resolved.
- No capacity headroom in the existing business — The company reports it 'maintained 100% capacity utilization through the year'. With the base plant already full, incremental growth cannot come from the existing asset and depends entirely on the new alloy steel capacity being commissioned.
- Execution and ramp-up risk on the Vaneera alloy steel project — The FY27 growth plan rests on one project: phase 1 of 100,000 MT per annum at Vaneera Industries' Ludhiana facility is stated only as 'ready to commission soon', with alloy steel facility work still 'underway' and no commissioning date, no rupee capex quantum and no funding plan disclosed in the report. The full 204,000 MT per annum licensed capacity is described as four times the company's current capacity, so the ramp is large relative to the existing business.
- Rising leverage after the acquisition — In its key-ratio disclosure the company explains the movement in its debt-equity ratio and debt service coverage ratio as being 'due to Increase in Borrowings during the year as compared to previous year' and 'Increase in the amount of Borrowings and their repayments during the year'. Borrowings rose from a near-debt-free base in a year in which the balance of the Vaneera consideration was paid, and further alloy-steel phases are still to be funded.
- Concentration in a narrow set of end markets and Tier-2 OEM customers — The value-added strategy deliberately concentrates the book on automotive, agri-machinery, engineering and precision industrial buyers, with the company 'established as a preferred vendor to Tier-2 OEM suppliers'. The same recurring-order relationships that support realisations also make the business sensitive to a downturn in auto and engineering demand; the report discloses no customer-concentration numbers.
- Single-location operations and a very small workforce — Both the existing business and the new alloy steel facility are at Ludhiana, Punjab, and the report states 'During the year, the company has employed 55 persons.' A single manufacturing location and a headcount that small leave the company exposed to site-level disruption and to key-person dependence on the promoter-family executive directors.

hero.oneLiner: Garg Furnace Limited is a Ludhiana-based induction-furnace steel maker that has shifted from commodity mild steel to chemistry-led, performance-graded steel, and now holds a 51% controlling stake in alloy-steel maker Vaneera Industries Limited.
